corrected terminal semantics, and `_assert_sql_flags` read all five
flags cleanly off the ~48 KB help text. The run then went further than
either prior attempt — the full sequence executed:


`D-P34.3-1` remains **OPEN** — the DEFERRALS row is untouched and no

## Blocker — TWO further latent defects surfaced (the leg never patches guards mid-leg)

### Defect C — the describe-shape blindness: evaluator reads `versioning.enabled`/`lifecycle.rule`; gcloud 583 emits `versioning_enabled`/`lifecycle_config`

`gcloud storage buckets describe --format=json` under SDK 583.0.0
emits the snake_case resource shape — top-level `versioning_enabled`
(bool), `lifecycle_config` ({rule:[…]}), `uniform_bucket_level_access`
— confirmed on all three buckets' pre- and post-state captures
(`protect/pre-20261124T221237Z/`, `protect/verify-20261124T221622Z/`).
Every bucket-state reader in `protect.sh` keys on the REST/JSON-API
camelCase shape instead:

- `_verify_python` (`ops/gcp/protect.sh` ~793–802):
  `v = d.get("versioning")` / `(d.get("lifecycle") or {}).get("rule")`
  → the six `qa-6` checks can **never** report OK under this gcloud —
  reproduced offline: `--verify --from-state` over the post-state dir
  prints the identical 6 DRIFTs while the same files contain the
  applied values (`protect-verify-fromstate-post.txt`).
- `_bucket_versioning_on` (~541), `_bucket_has_our_rule` (~558),
  `_bucket_rule_count` (~579) read the same absent keys → always
  false / always 0 → not idempotent (a re-run re-applies both
  updates; harmless in itself) — **but `_bucket_rule_count`
  always-0 makes the refuse-to-overwrite foreign-lifecycle guard
  (598–602) vacuous**: on a bucket carrying foreign rules it would
  have silently `--lifecycle-file`-replaced them. This leg was safe
  only because all three pre-state captures verifiably show
  `lifecycle_config: null`.
- `tests/ops/test_protect_iac.py` fixtures record the
  `versioning`/`lifecycle` shape, so the offline `--from-state` suite
  is green both directions while the live describe emits the other —
  the defect was unobservable until the first real apply landed the
  fields (this run).

`evaluator-key-sites.txt` lists the exact sites.

### Defect D — the QA-7 post-check cannot see through the GCS edge cache: a cached 200 read as "removal did not take" → premature auto-rollback

`index.html` on `sig-web` carries `cache-control: public,
max-age=3600` and GCS edge-caches publicly served objects. Timeline
(`protect-apply.txt`, `bucket-url-headers.txt`):

- ~22:15:0xZ — `remove-iam-policy-binding` succeeded; the printed
  policy shows `roles/storage.objectViewer` holding ONLY
  `serviceAccount:sig-web-rt@…` — **allUsers verifiably absent**. The
  bucket has `uniform_bucket_level_access: true` and the object ACL is
  empty (`bucket-iam-config.txt`, `object-index-acl.txt`), so IAM is
  the sole authorisation mechanism — a live anonymous 200 was
  impossible in that window.
- seconds later — the script's direct-URL check got `200` on a
  response carrying **`Age`** (captured minutes later: `age: 933`,
  `date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 22:00:40 GMT`, `expires: 23:00:40 GMT`) —
  i.e. a cache-fill that predates the removal by ~15 min, kept warm
  by earlier baseline fetches and organic traffic.
- the script read the cached 200 as "bucket still publicly readable —
  IAM removal did not take" and ran `_rollback_web_iam`, re-adding
  `allUsers:objectViewer` (verified present, `iam-sig-web-post.txt`).

The machinery executed its specified stop rule faithfully; the defect
is that the signal is unsound — an edge-cached 200 cannot evidence
public readability within `max-age` of the last public fetch, and
`index.html` is re-fetched by real traffic constantly, so the entry
effectively never drains. **Minimal reproducer:** with `index.html`
warm in the GCS edge cache, `--apply iam` removes the binding (takes —
printed policy), the immediate `curl` on the direct URL returns a
cached 200 with an `Age` header, and the leg rolls back — every time,
inside any window where the object was publicly fetched in the prior
hour.

### What unblocks this leg (for the operator / orchestrator)

1. Fix the describe-shape parsing in `_verify_python` and the three
   `_bucket_*` readers to normalise the live snake_case shape
   (`versioning_enabled`, `lifecycle_config`, including the
   camelCase→snake path `norm()` already walks), with a
   `test_protect_iac.py` fixture captured from a real
   `describe --format=json` payload so the offline suite exercises the
   live shape. Restoring `_bucket_rule_count`'s eyesight also restores
   the foreign-rule refuse-guard.
2. Make the QA-7 post-check cache-sound: e.g. treat a 200 carrying an
   `Age` header as cache, not evidence; probe an object the cache
   cannot hold (a never-published name: 403 proves private, 404
   proves public); or poll until the cached entry expires. Machinery
   decision for the fix ticket — never a leg-runner edit.
3. Re-dispatch `r11/P34.3-live-<n>` under the go's authority: the
   instance and bucket legs will read-then-SKIP (once the readers can
   see — today they re-apply harmlessly), and only QA-7 remains
   substantively owed. Note the interaction: even with the readers
   fixed, defect D blocks `11 OK` inside any hour where `index.html`
   saw public traffic — both fixes are needed before the next leg.
